# Proposal: AI Governance Academy Implementation Accelerator

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Implementation Accelerator, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client is at a piloting stage of AI maturity, with three known AI use cases:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

An internal audit finding dated June 2026 recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems. The Client lists the EU AI Act and GDPR as regulatory drivers. The Client has also stated an intent to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, though the start date is not fixed.

The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The Client has stated three constraints that shape this work:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

## 2. Why an Intensive AIMS Foundation Build Fits

The Implementation Accelerator is a five-day intensive working session. It establishes the foundation of an Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) and fits the Client's situation for four reasons.

**It answers the audit finding directly.** The June 2026 finding concerns the absence of an AI system inventory. The Accelerator produces that inventory on Day 2 as a named, Client-owned artifact. The Client's internal audit function can then review it.

**It matches the ISO/IEC 42001 intent without overreaching.** ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, with no fixed date. The Accelerator structures every artifact for future conformity work. This is readiness work. It does not promise certification, audit results or any conformity outcome. Building the foundation now means the Client starts its ISO/IEC 42001 work with a charter, inventory, risk register, policy set and evidence model already drafted.

**It attaches to what the Client already runs.** Each artifact is designed to attach to the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, the ISO 9001 quality management system and the internal audit function, rather than stand alone. Our notes name these systems but not their component registers, procedures or records. Specific attachment points are therefore `Unknown` until the build team confirms them during the week.

**It fits the timeline and budget as stated.** A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. The Accelerator is a fixed five-day engagement at US$25,000, which sits within the US$80,000 approved for this fiscal year. Its output is concrete enough to show what is in place relative to the stated Q2 2027 objective.

The regulatory content in the Accelerator, including any mapping of the Client's use cases to the EU AI Act or GDPR, is orientation only. This includes risk classification of the visual inspection pilot and data handling in the chatbot. Any item with legal effect carries the note: confirm with external counsel.

The week is guided by three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 3. The Five-Day Build Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

The sequence follows two dependencies: the charter comes before policies, and the inventory comes before the risk register.

**Day 1: Governance Charter and Roles.**
- The build team drafts the AIMS governance charter: purpose, scope, roles, decision rights and meeting cadence.
- Scope covers the three known use cases.
- The roles model draws on the functions represented in the build team.
- The charter records the German works council consultation requirement as a governance constraint. Whether a given system touches production staff is a determination the Client makes and records.
- Executive checkpoint attendance opens the day.

**Day 2: AI System Inventory and Classification.**
- The team builds the inventory schema and classification scheme.
- The chatbot, visual inspection pilot and planned sales forecasting are entered as the first three records.
- Classification fields include lifecycle state, deployment location, data categories and data residency, so the EU data constraint can be recorded and checked per system.
- Field values the Client has not yet confirmed are entered as `Unknown`.

**Day 3: Risk and Impact Assessment plus Risk Register.**
- Using the Day 2 inventory, the team applies a risk and impact assessment method to each system.
- The team stands up the AI risk register.
- Seeded risk statements are drafts for Client validation.
- The register is designed to sit alongside existing risk practice under the ISMS and quality management system, with specific attachment points `Unknown` until confirmed.

**Day 4: Core Policies and Operating Procedures.**
- Policies are written under the authority of the Day 1 charter.
- The set covers acceptable use, AI lifecycle governance, vendor and supplier governance, incident response and change management.
- Vendor and supplier governance addresses the EU customer data constraint.
- Lifecycle and change management address the path from pilot to production.

**Day 5: Evidence Model, Implementation Priorities and Executive Readout.**
- The team builds an evidence index that maps each artifact to the assurance question it answers, in a form the internal audit function can use.
- The team sets out prioritized implementation steps.
- The week closes with the executive readout.

## 4. Artifacts the Client Owns at Close

Every artifact is delivered in the Client's document system and owned by the Client. Each carries a status of draft, reviewed or adopted.

1. AIMS Governance Charter
2. Roles and Decision Rights Matrix
3. AI System Inventory, seeded with the chatbot, visual inspection pilot and planned sales forecasting
4. AI System Classification Scheme
5. AI Risk and Impact Assessment Method
6. AI Risk Register, with seeded risk statements marked as drafts for Client validation
7. AI Acceptable Use Policy
8. AI Lifecycle Governance Policy
9. AI Vendor and Supplier Governance Policy
10. AI Incident Response Procedure
11. AI Change Management Procedure
12. Evidence Index
13. Implementation Priorities and 90-Day Plan
14. Executive Readout
15. Regulatory Orientation Note covering the EU AI Act and GDPR (orientation only; confirm with external counsel)

The work draws on these frameworks:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)
- AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards), as the board-layer reference

## 5. Team Composition Asked of the Client

We ask the Client to designate a build team spanning the following roles for all five days:

- General Counsel
- CISO
- Head of Quality
- Head of Data
- German plant manager
- Two internal auditors

We also ask the Client to name the executives who will attend the checkpoints on Day 1 and Day 5. These attendees are `Unknown` at this stage.

Ahead of Day 1, we ask the build team to identify the existing ISMS and quality management system documents the artifacts should attach to. Any of these not available by then will be recorded as `Unknown` and carried forward.

## 6. Logistics and Price

- **Duration:** 5 consecutive working days.
- **Format:** live virtual working sessions with structured build time.
- **Price:** US$25,000.
- **Proposed dates:** `Unknown`, to be agreed with the Client.

## 7. Next Step

We propose a short scoping call with you to confirm three things:

- the build team members
- the executive checkpoint attendees
- candidate dates for the five days

Following that call, we will issue the five-day workplan and the Artifact Register for the Client's review.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
